candidates.content_text:
The Opportunity:
Maitland City Council's Pathways program is a fantastic way to kick-start your career and gain professional experience in local government!
Commencing in January 2027, for a period of two years, we have two exciting opportunities for Graduate Civil Engineers to join our organisation.
In this role, you will undertake a graduate program developed specifically for you, giving you exposure to a range of civil engineering functions for the investigation and delivery of civil and recreation infrastructure projects undertaken by Council. These duties are going to help you develop a solid foundation to your civil engineering career.
About you:
To be successful in this role you will possess:
- Degree level qualifications in Civil engineering in the previous two years or completion of degree by January 2027
- Contemporary industry knowledge of civil engineering areas
- Experience and understanding in project support and the research, analysis and presentation of information
- Current Class C driver's licence
Benefits:
This Graduate position is temporary full time (two-year contract) with a commencing salary of $1,414.58 weekly, plus 12% superannuation. Graduates will also have access to Council's great staff benefits including:
- Flexible work arrangements
- One extra week of "My Leave" a year (to use how you like!)
- Ongoing training and development
- Fitness Passport
- Healthy Employee Program
To apply:
To apply for this opportunity, please click 'Apply Now' and submit your resume and cover letter.
Questions:
To viw the role charter click 'Apply Now'. If after reading the role charter you have any questions, please contact the recruitment team at Recruitment@maitland.nsw.gov.au
More information regarding Council's Pathways Program can be viewed via https://www.maitland.nsw.gov.au/pathways-program.
Applications close: Sunday 25th October 2027
Only candidates with current Australian work rights (Australian citizens, permanent residents, NZ citizens with a current passport, valid work visa) will be considered.
What happens next?
Once applications close, we will review all candidates' details against the role requirements and will be back in touch with you to advise the status of your application.
Please note, prior to an offer of employment being made, recommended candidates will be required to undertake a medical assessment (including drug and alcohol testing). Council also completes a range of other pre-employment checks which may include reference checks, psychometric testing or a criminal history check. For more information about the recruitment process, visit the "Jobs at Council" page on our website.
Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
Maitland City Council is dedicated to providing a workplace that is inclusive and supportive and is reflective of the diverse community we serve. We support equal opportunities for all employees, and encourage applications from people from all cultures, nationalities, identities, and abilities. We believe all employees have the right to feel valued, respected and heard. If you have any special considerations or accessibility requirements, please let us know in the recruitment process how we are able to meet your needs.
 If you require special assistance, or have any questions about the recruitment process please contact us for a confidential conversation (Recruitment@maitland.nsw.gov.au)

About the role
Ground Civil is seeking an experienced Civil Designer to join our West Perth office, with strong experience in subdivision and land development design.
You will work on a variety of civil and land development projects across Western Australia, taking designs from initial concept through detailed design and authority approval. The role will suit a practical designer who is confident in Civil 3D and can work independently while collaborating closely with our engineering team.
Key responsibilities
- Prepare subdivision and land development designs using AutoCAD Civil 3D
- Design roads, earthworks, stormwater drainage, sewer and water infrastructure
- Prepare detailed design and construction drawings
- Develop Civil 3D surfaces, alignments, profiles, corridors and earthworks models
- Coordinate designs with surveyors, engineers and other consultants
- Assist with local government, Water Corporation and other authority approvals
- Respond to design review comments and coordinate amendments through to approval
- Ensure designs and documentation are accurate, practical and compliant with applicable standards
About you
- Demonstrated civil design experience in subdivision and land development
- Strong proficiency in AutoCAD Civil 3D
- Practical experience in road, drainage, earthworks and utility design
- Australian civil design experience
- WA subdivision and land development experience will be highly regarded
- Familiarity with WA approval processes and relevant authority requirements will be highly regarded
- Ability to work independently and manage design tasks efficiently
- Strong attention to detail and ability to produce high-quality construction documentation
- Good communication and coordination skills
Why join Ground Civil?
- Work directly on a diverse range of subdivision and land development projects
- Be involved across the design process rather than working on only one component
- Work closely with experienced engineers in our West Perth office
- Opportunity to take ownership of designs and develop broader project experience
- Professional and supportive small-team environment

We have an exciting opportunity for a Graduate Civil Engineer to join our Beerburrum to Nambour (B2N) Rail Upgrade project.
This a major infrastructure project transforming the North Coast Line on the Sunshine Coast. The project includes rail duplication, new and upgraded transport infrastructure, improved road overpasses and enhanced signalling systems, all aimed at increasing capacity and reliability across the network. Throughout the program, you'll be supported by experienced mentors, participate in structured development workshops, and connect with a national network of graduates and professionals who are invested in your success.
What's in it for you?
- Work on a landmark civil infrastructure project from day one
- Gain exposure to multiple disciplines across project delivery
- Receive structured mentoring, coaching and development support
- Learn from experienced industry leaders and subject matter experts
- Build a strong professional network across projects and regions
- Be part of a collaborative, supportive and high-performing team culture
- Access career opportunities within the VINCI Group, a global leader in construction, infrastructure and concessions

- Practical experience through internships, vacation programs, placements or other employment
- A genuine passion for civil construction and infrastructure projects
- A positive attitude and willingness to learn from experienced industry professionals
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- A commitment to safety, collaboration and creating a positive team culture
- Flexibility to travel or relocate as opportunities arise throughout your career
Most importantly, you're ready to take the next step, embrace new challenges and build a rewarding career delivering projects that make a lasting impact on communities across Australia.

Our Business
Working at TasWater isn't just a job; it's an opportunity to deliver social, environmental, and economic benefits for Tasmania today, and tomorrow. 
Our talented workforce of over 950 employees keeps Tasmania thriving by providing exceptional water and sewerage services to over 460,000 customers every day. 
We have a bold and ambitious future, inspired by our vision to unlock water’s full potential, and centred on our customers and communities, our people and partners, the environment, and our collective water future.   
Over the coming 4 years we’re investing $1.2 billion to ensure a safe and secure water future for a growing Tasmania, and we will make great steps towards our aspirations of net zero carbon emissions and towards zero waste. Visit our website or YouTube channel to learn more. 
The Role
We're looking for a motivated and technically capable Engineer Dam Infrastructure to join us on a permanent full-time basis. Reporting to the Dam Infrastructure Manager, you'll play a key role in supporting the safe, compliant and efficient management of TasWater's dam infrastructure assets across Tasmania.  
This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to dam safety engineering, asset performance, compliance and continuous improvement initiatives that help protect our communities, environment and critical infrastructure. Working closely with engineers, operators, specialists and external stakeholders, you'll help deliver engineering solutions that support both regulatory obligations and long-term asset outcomes.  
As part of the team, you'll work across TasWater's diverse portfolio of 304 dams, including concrete weirs, earthen embankment dams, and concrete arch and buttress dams. Spread across some of Tasmania's most spectacular and remote locations, these assets offer a rare opportunity to blend engineering expertise with field-based work while helping safeguard critical water infrastructure for future generations. 
In this role, you will: 
- Deliver dam safety engineering support, solutions and improvements to achieve compliance and asset performance outcomes. 
- Provide project management and technical oversight for dam infrastructure programs and improvement works. 
- Monitor and analyse dam asset performance to support asset, workforce and community safety. 
- Research, analyse and report on engineering issues, developing practical and compliant solutions. 
- Schedule and coordinate compliance, surveillance and inspection activities. 
- Prepare and maintain engineering documentation including reports, plans, specifications and business cases. 
- Support emergency preparedness activities, including participation in dam safety emergency exercises. 
- Build effective relationships with operational teams, contractors, consultants and industry stakeholders to achieve organisational outcomes. 
For a full copy of the position description, please visit our website: www.taswater.com.au
What we're looking for
We're seeking an engineering professional who combines sound technical knowledge with strong problem-solving and stakeholder engagement capabilities. 
To thrive in this role, you’ll bring: 
- A degree in Engineering or equivalent demonstrated experience in dam safety asset management functions. 
- A sound understanding of engineering concepts and principles relating to water and sewerage infrastructure. 
- Strong engineering analysis and problem-solving skills. 
- Excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills. 
- The ability to interpret technical plans, drawings and specifications. 
- Proficiency in engineering software and computer-based systems. 
- Knowledge of relevant health and safety legislation, regulations and codes of practice. 
- A current Class C driver's licence. 
Highly regarded: 
- Project management experience or qualifications. 
- Full professional membership of a relevant engineering association.

We are continuing to build an inclusive workplace and workforce that truly represents the Tasmanian community that we serve. We value diversity in all its many forms and welcome a range of perspectives and identities to enrich the way we work and what we do. 
We take pride in being acknowledged as an employer of choice for women by WORK180. Visit the Work180 website to view our benefits and policies, such as 18 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents regardless of tenure and with full superannuation contributions. We’re continuing to work on future benefits through a dedicated Employee Experience team. 
The Details

The position may require travel throughout Tasmania, site inspections, work in both indoor and outdoor environments, and participation in after-hours work or an on-call roster as required to support business operations. 
Ready to apply? Simply include a CV/resume and a 1–2-page cover letter telling us how your experience matches "What we are looking for" and how you connect to our TasWater values and vision.    
If you want to learn more about this role, please contact Gemma Casey - Dam Infrastructure Manager at 0436 624 732 or via email at Gemma.Casey@taswater.com.au  
If you need assistance in applying, please contact Roly Srivastava – Talent Acquisition Officer at 0498 608 719 or via email at Roly.Srivastava@taswater.com.au

- Salary continuance insurance

- An inclusive and diverse group of colleagues who happily share knowledge

- Modern office | Walking distance from train stations | Red Cat bus
- Global, progressive company with industry leading innovation and cutting-edge technology

candidates.abstract: Sparkling new Estimator seat in a fast-growing mining services division. $150K to $190K + 20% STI, Perth CBD, and a real say in what wins.
bullets: $150K to $190K base + 20% STI on top
Brand new role: you own civil pricing from day one
Civil favoured. Mining, haulage or crushing welcome
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
How many years' experience do you have as an Estimator?

What's your expected annual base salary?

Are you willing to undergo a pre-employment medical check?
Do you live in Perth?
Do you have estimating experience in the civil mining sector?
Have you worked in the crushing & haulage space?
candidates.content_text:
Last week the RBA lifted rates for the fourth time this year, citing "upside risks to inflation". Cue half the country suddenly discovering escalation. Estimators have been quietly pricing that risk in since about March.
 I'm Andrew from Itch, and I'm after someone who sees the risk before the headline does. So I've laid this one out the way you'd want any submission to land on your desk.
 The rates
 - $150K to $190K base, depending on experience
 - Plus a 20% STI on top
 - Permanent, Perth CBD based
 - A brand new role. Nobody walked out of this seat, it's never had anyone in it
 The scope 
A mining services division that's grown hard over the last three years. The person who built it went on to hire a Tender Manager, a Business Development Manager and a Business Analyst, and between them they've been winning work. Pricing used to be shared between the founder and the Tender Manager, but the founder has since stepped up into an executive role and can't stay on the tools.
That leaves a gap with your name on it, specifically civil pricing. It's the one capability the business doesn't have in house yet, which means you won't be the fourth opinion on a number. You'll be the number.
Inclusions
 - Building civil cost models for mining clients: earthworks, drainage, TSF dam construction and lifts, structures and the civil infrastructure around them
 - Reading the tender pack properly (scope, drawings, specs, geotech reports, conditions of contract) and telling the operations team the pros and cons before anyone commits
 - Getting out to site for tender meetings to see the access, the ground and the constraints for yourself, instead of pricing from a PDF
 - Standing up in the room and presenting the submission to the client. Your number, your pitch
 - Repricing, variations and rate reviews on live sites, finding the savings that keep the business competitive
 - Post-award reviews of estimated versus actual cost. You'll actually find out if you were right, and feed it back into the models
 - A genuine say in which jobs are worth chasing, with BD, tender and analysis support already in the room
 Exclusions
 - A 40-person estimating department where your number gets rewritten twice before anyone sends it
 - Big personalities. The team's straightforward and good to work with
 - Being a spreadsheet operator for someone else's strategy
 Assumptions
 - 3+ years in estimating, and 3+ years across civil construction, haulage or mining
 - Civil pricing is the background they'll look at first. Not civil? If you've estimated mining, haulage or crushing work, still talk to me. Strength in one area plus a keen interest in the others is genuinely fine
 - You know civil methods, materials and cost drivers, and can read civil drawings, specs and geotech reports without a translator
 - Strong in Excel and MS Project, plus civil estimating software
 - Bonus points for an engineering, construction management or QS qualification, or a Cert IV in Estimating or Civil Construction. Not essential
 - You'd rather be right than fast, but you can be both when the tender closes Friday at 2pm
 This business wants someone who's choosing them for the work, the influence and the growth, not for a bidding war or counter offer
 Submission 
Hit apply with your CV, and add a line about the biggest or trickiest civil job you've priced. I'll give you a call for a confidential chat about the team, the work pipeline, and where this role goes as the division keeps growing.
How many estimators does it take to change a light bulb? One, plus 10% contingency, subject to site conditions. If you laughed, you're probably who I'm looking for.
**ONLY APPLICANTS LIVING IN PERTH WITH FULL AUSTRALIAN WORK RIGHTS WILL BE CONSIDERED**
candidates.teaser: Sparkling new Estimator seat in a fast-growing mining services division. $150K to $190K + 20% STI, Perth CBD, and a real say in what wins.
